situation:
You are a young adult who needs a reliable car to get to work, and you are still carrying a $2,300 balance on your first credit card at 24 percent. You have an appointment with an insurance agent (judge) at GRANITE PASS INSURANCE AGENCY.

A three-year lease on a new compact runs $290 a month, and the leasing company requires you to carry the $500-deductible policy for all three years, which the agency quotes at $1,380 a year. A loan on a four-year-old version of the same car runs $340 a month and lets you choose a $1,500 deductible at $1,020 a year.

Leasing means paying that $1,380 premium every year whether or not a crash ever happens. The loan takes an $1,800 down payment that would otherwise pay off most of the credit card balance, and leaves you covering the first $1,500 of any repair yourself. Your older brother has offered to co-sign the loan and would be on the hook if you missed a payment.

The insurance agent (judge) wants you to rank what matters most to you over the next three years, compare what each choice would cost you in a good year and in a bad one, and recommend one. The agent (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.

Business background is the same as the situation above.

You want the participant to rank what matters most to them over the next three years, to compare what each choice would cost in a good year and in a bad one, and to recommend one.

You will begin by greeting the participant and asking to hear their ideas. During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: If you go the other way, what does that cost you?
